mean: to let one's mind run wild with idle or groundless thoughts
lit: to think wildly and imagine at random

use.how: Used as a verb, very often in 别胡思乱想 to calm someone who is worrying for no reason. Said of a person's own wandering, anxious thoughts.

near.diff: 异想天开 is a fanciful, unrealistic idea or plan; 胡思乱想 is aimless, often anxious thinking with no basis.

cue: Your friend lies awake picturing every way tomorrow's interview could go wrong. You tell her to stop and get some sleep.

ctx.s: 别{胡思乱想}了，早点睡吧。
ctx.en: Stop letting your imagination run away with you and get some sleep.

ctx.s: 我一晚上没回电话，妈妈一个人在家{胡思乱想}。
ctx.en: I didn't return her calls all evening, so Mum sat at home imagining the worst.

ctx.s: 体检结果还没出来，你先别{胡思乱想}，等医生说了再讲。
ctx.en: The test results aren't out yet, so don't go imagining things; wait for the doctor.

ctx.s: “他是不是不喜欢我了？”“你想多了，别{胡思乱想}。”
ctx.en: "Has he stopped liking me?" "You're overthinking it. Don't torture yourself with ideas like that."

ctx.s: 人一闲下来，就容易{胡思乱想}。
ctx.en: When people have nothing to do, their minds easily start to wander into worries.

ctx.s: 考试前一天晚上，她躺在床上{胡思乱想}，怎么也睡不着。
ctx.en: The night before the exam she lay in bed with her thoughts racing and couldn't fall asleep.

bad.s: 他是个科学家，每天在实验室里{胡思乱想}新发明。
bad.en: (meant: he spends his days imagining new inventions)
bad.why: It disparages idle, groundless thoughts; it cannot describe creative or productive thinking.

bad.s: 这个计划太{胡思乱想}了，根本行不通。
bad.en: (meant: this plan is too unrealistic)
bad.why: It is what a person does in their head, not a quality of a plan; a plan that is wildly unrealistic calls for yì xiǎng tiān kāi.

mean: again and again, time after time

use.how: Adverbial before a verb: 我三番五次提醒他。 Said of one person repeating the same act, often a request, warning or nuisance, usually with impatience.

near.diff: 接二连三 is about events following one another quickly; 三番五次 is about someone doing the same thing over and over.

cue: You reminded your roommate again and again to lock the front door, and he still left it open last night.

ctx.s: 我{三番五次}提醒他带伞，他还是忘了。
ctx.en: I reminded him to take an umbrella time after time, and he still forgot.

ctx.s: 老板{三番五次}找他谈话，他才答应留下来。
ctx.en: Only after the boss talked to him again and again did he agree to stay.

ctx.s: 楼上的邻居{三番五次}在半夜放音乐，大家都很生气。
ctx.en: The upstairs neighbour keeps playing music in the middle of the night, and everyone is angry.

ctx.s: 你怎么又迟到了？我已经{三番五次}跟你说过了！
ctx.en: Late again? I've told you over and over!

ctx.s: 这家公司{三番五次}邀请她加入，都被她婉言谢绝了。
ctx.en: The company invited her to join again and again, and each time she politely declined.

ctx.s: 他{三番五次}地向物业反映，问题却一直没有解决。
ctx.en: He complained to the building management time after time, but the problem was never fixed.

bad.s: 地球{三番五次}地绕着太阳转。
bad.en: (meant: the earth keeps going round the sun)
bad.why: It is about a person repeating a deliberate act, not a regular natural cycle.

bad.s: 他每天早上{三番五次}地刷牙。
bad.en: (meant: he brushes his teeth every morning)
bad.why: It marks repetition beyond what is expected, usually requests or warnings, not a normal daily routine.

use.how: Adverbial or object about speaking: 三言两语就说清楚了, or negated: 不是三言两语能说清的. Said of how briefly something is or can be said.

near.diff: 一言难尽 says a matter is too complex or painful to tell at all; 三言两语 simply means a few words, which may or may not be enough.

cue: Your colleague settled a long argument in the meeting with just a couple of short sentences. How did he do it?

ctx.s: 这件事很简单，{三言两语}就能说清楚。
ctx.en: This is simple; it can be explained in a couple of sentences.

ctx.s: 他{三言两语}就把哭闹的孩子哄笑了。
ctx.en: With just a few words he had the crying child laughing.

ctx.s: 这个问题很复杂，不是{三言两语}能讲明白的。
ctx.en: This problem is complicated; it can't be explained in a few words.

ctx.s: 经理只用了{三言两语}，就让会议回到了正题。
ctx.en: With only a few words the manager brought the meeting back on topic.

ctx.s: 临走前，她{三言两语}交代了几件事，就匆匆出门了。
ctx.en: Before leaving she gave a few quick instructions and hurried out the door.

ctx.s: 他在信里只写了{三言两语}，说自己一切都好。
ctx.en: He wrote only a few lines in the letter, saying that all was well.

bad.s: 他是个{三言两语}的人，从来不爱说话。
bad.en: (meant: he is a man of few words)
bad.why: It describes a brief utterance, not a person's character; for a quiet man of few words use chén mò guǎ yán.

bad.s: 这本书写得很{三言两语}，读起来很轻松。
bad.en: (meant: the book is concisely written)
bad.why: It is not an adjective and cannot take hěn; concise writing is jiǎnjié.

lit: to think three times and then act

story.text: The Analects records that Ji Wenzi, a minister of the state of Lu, always thought three times before he acted. When Confucius heard of it he remarked: twice is enough. The phrase 'think three times, then act' became a saying that now simply advises careful thought before acting, though Confucius himself was hinting that Ji Wenzi overdid it.

use.how: Usually advice before a decision: 你要三思而行, 还是三思而行吧, or a habit: 做事总是三思而行. Also said in the full form 三思而后行.

near.diff: 深思熟虑 describes careful thought already given (经过深思熟虑); 三思而行 is advice to think before you act.

cue: Your cousin wants to quit a stable job tomorrow, on impulse, to open a café. What do you advise before he hands in his notice?

ctx.s: 辞职是大事，你最好{三思而行}。
ctx.en: Quitting is a big step; you'd better think it over carefully first.

ctx.s: 爷爷常对我们说，凡事要{三思而行}。
ctx.en: Grandpa always told us to think things through before acting.

ctx.s: “我打算把房子卖了去创业。”“这么大的决定，还是{三思而行}吧。”
ctx.en: "I'm planning to sell the flat and start a business." "A decision that big, you should think twice."

ctx.s: 网上投资陷阱很多，大家一定要{三思而行}。
ctx.en: There are many online investment traps, so everyone should think carefully before acting.

ctx.s: 他年轻时吃过冲动的亏，从那以后做事总是{三思而行}。
ctx.en: He paid for being impulsive when he was young, and ever since he has always thought before acting.

ctx.s: 签合同之前，律师提醒她{三思而行}，别急着签字。
ctx.en: Before she signed the contract, her lawyer reminded her to think it over and not rush to sign.

bad.s: 经过{三思而行}，他终于做出了决定。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he finally decided)
bad.why: It is advice or a habit, not a noun for thought that can follow jīngguò; say jīngguò shēn sī shú lǜ.

bad.s: 他{三思而行}地把这本书看了三遍。
bad.en: (meant: he read the book carefully three times)
bad.why: The three is not a count of repeats; it means being careful before taking an action.

lit: of ten grabs, nine hold firm

use.how: Predicate or 是…的 about the likely outcome of an exam, deal or match: 这次比赛我们十拿九稳。 Also said of confidence that turns out misplaced.

near.diff: 万无一失 says nothing at all can go wrong, often of safety measures; 十拿九稳 is a confident forecast that something will succeed.
胸有成竹 is about having a ready plan in mind; 十拿九稳 is about the odds of the result.

cue: Your team leads by twenty points with two minutes left, and a teammate says the win is as good as in the bag.

ctx.s: 这次考试我准备得很充分，及格是{十拿九稳}的。
ctx.en: I've prepared thoroughly for this exam; passing is a sure thing.

ctx.s: “这笔生意你有几成把握？”“放心吧，{十拿九稳}。”
ctx.en: "How sure are you of closing this deal?" "Don't worry, it's in the bag."

ctx.s: 以她的成绩，考上这所大学应该{十拿九稳}。
ctx.en: With her grades, getting into this university should be practically certain.

ctx.s: 他以为这场比赛{十拿九稳}，没想到最后输了。
ctx.en: He thought the match was a sure win, but in the end they lost.

ctx.s: 我们才领先一个球，现在说{十拿九稳}还太早。
ctx.en: We're only one goal ahead; it's too early to call it a sure win.

ctx.s: 教练觉得这场球{十拿九稳}，就让主力球员休息了。
ctx.en: The coach thought the game was a certain win, so he rested his key players.

bad.s: 这座桥修得{十拿九稳}，可以用很多年。
bad.en: (meant: the bridge is very solidly built)
bad.why: It forecasts the success of an attempt, not physical sturdiness; a solid bridge is jiēshi or láogù.

bad.s: 我对他的人品{十拿九稳}。
bad.en: (meant: I fully trust his character)
bad.why: It is about the likely outcome of an attempt, not about trusting a person; say xìndeguò, to trust.

mean: absolutely true, every word of it (of a report or claim)
lit: a thousand times true, ten thousand times certain

use.how: Predicate or a reply on its own, insisting that news, a fact or a claim is true: 这消息千真万确。

cue: Your friend refuses to believe the shy new classmate won the speech contest. You were there and insist it really happened.

ctx.s: 这个消息{千真万确}，是我亲耳听到的。
ctx.en: This news is absolutely true; I heard it with my own ears.

ctx.s: “他真的要出国了？”“{千真万确}，机票都买好了。”
ctx.en: "Is he really going abroad?" "Absolutely, he's already bought the ticket."

ctx.s: 我说的每一句话都是{千真万确}的，你可以去查。
ctx.en: Every word I've said is true; you can check.

ctx.s: 起初没人相信她中了大奖，可这件事{千真万确}。
ctx.en: At first nobody believed she had won the big prize, but it was absolutely true.

ctx.s: 报道里说的那些事，难道都是{千真万确}的吗？
ctx.en: Is everything in that report really, completely true?

ctx.s: 调查结果表明，他当晚就在现场，这一点{千真万确}。
ctx.en: The investigation established beyond doubt that he was at the scene that night.

bad.s: 他是一个{千真万确}的人，从不撒谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an honest person who never lies)
bad.why: It says a statement or fact is true, not that a person is honest; an honest person is chéngshí.

bad.s: 你放心，我明天{千真万确}会来。
bad.en: (meant: don't worry, I will definitely come tomorrow)
bad.why: It insists that a fact or report is true; it is not an adverb for a promise. To promise, say yídìng huì lái.

mean: all sorts of strange and bizarre things
lit: a thousand oddities and a hundred strange things

use.how: Attributive with 的 or predicate, about many things, shapes or questions that are odd: 千奇百怪的石头, 形状千奇百怪.

near.diff: 五花八门 stresses a great variety of kinds; 千奇百怪 stresses that the things are strange and odd.

cue: On a reef dive you see fish shaped like boxes, needles and balloons, each odder than the last. How do you describe them?

ctx.s: 海底有很多{千奇百怪}的鱼。
ctx.en: There are all kinds of weird and wonderful fish on the seabed.

ctx.s: 这座山上的石头形状{千奇百怪}，有的像动物，有的像人。
ctx.en: The rocks on this mountain come in all sorts of bizarre shapes; some look like animals, some like people.

ctx.s: 孩子们总会问一些{千奇百怪}的问题，比如鱼会不会做梦。
ctx.en: Children are always asking the strangest questions, like whether fish dream.

ctx.s: 昨天夜里我做了好多{千奇百怪}的梦。
ctx.en: Last night I had a whole string of bizarre dreams.

ctx.s: 博物馆里的古代乐器长得{千奇百怪}，我根本看不出是怎么演奏的。
ctx.en: The ancient instruments in the museum come in such bizarre shapes that I couldn't tell how they were played.

ctx.s: “这家店卖什么？”“全是些{千奇百怪}的小玩意儿，好多我都叫不出名字。”
ctx.en: "What does this shop sell?" "All sorts of odd little gadgets; I can't even name half of them."

bad.s: 他这个人{千奇百怪}的，谁都不理。
bad.en: (meant: he is a strange man who ignores everyone)
bad.why: It describes a mass of many different odd things, not one person's eccentric character; an odd person is gǔguài.

bad.s: 这家超市商品{千奇百怪}，日用品一应俱全。
bad.en: (meant: the supermarket has a full range of goods)
bad.why: It implies the goods are bizarre; a full range of ordinary goods is yīng yǒu jìn yǒu.

mean: one after another in quick succession
lit: the second follows on, the third joins after

use.how: Adverbial, often with 地, before verbs like 发生, 传来, 出现: 事故接二连三地发生. Said of separate events, often bad ones, coming close together.

near.diff: 三番五次 is someone repeating the same act; 接二连三 is separate events following one after another.
络绎不绝 is a steady stream of people or vehicles; 接二连三 is a series of separate happenings.

cue: Within one week your car broke down, your phone was stolen and your landlord raised the rent. How did the troubles arrive?

ctx.s: 好消息{接二连三}地传来，大家都很高兴。
ctx.en: Good news kept coming in, one piece after another, and everyone was delighted.

ctx.s: 最近家里{接二连三}地出事，妈妈都累病了。
ctx.en: One thing after another has gone wrong at home lately, and Mum has worn herself out.

ctx.s: 比赛刚开始，对方就{接二连三}地进了好几个球。
ctx.en: Right after kick-off the other side scored several goals in quick succession.

ctx.s: 这个路口{接二连三}发生车祸，交警决定加装红绿灯。
ctx.en: After one accident after another at this junction, the traffic police decided to put in lights.

ctx.s: “你今天怎么了？”“别提了，{接二连三}地出状况。”
ctx.en: "What's up with you today?" "Don't ask. One mishap after another."

ctx.s: 新店开张后，订单{接二连三}地涌来，员工忙得团团转。
ctx.en: After the new shop opened, orders poured in one after another and the staff were run off their feet.

bad.s: 他{接二连三}地爱了她二十年。
bad.en: (meant: he loved her without a break for twenty years)
bad.why: It is about separate events in quick succession, not one continuous state over a long time.

bad.s: 教室里学生{接二连三}，座位都坐满了。
bad.en: (meant: the classroom is packed with students)
bad.why: It describes events following in time, not a large number of people present at once.

mean: all the streets and alleys of a town

use.how: A place noun, as subject (大街小巷都…) or object of 传遍, 走遍, 穿过: 歌声传遍了大街小巷. Means everywhere in a town.

near.diff: 家喻户晓 means known in every household; 大街小巷 names the places, every street in town, where something is seen or heard.

cue: During the festival, red lanterns hang over every road and lane in the city, from the main avenue to the tiniest alley.

ctx.s: 春节快到了，{大街小巷}都挂起了红灯笼。
ctx.en: Spring Festival is near, and red lanterns hang in every street and lane.

ctx.s: 这首歌一夜之间传遍了{大街小巷}。
ctx.en: Overnight this song could be heard on every street in town.

ctx.s: 我小时候常和朋友骑车穿过城里的{大街小巷}。
ctx.en: As a child I often rode my bike with friends through all the streets and alleys of the town.

ctx.s: 下了一夜大雪，{大街小巷}一片白茫茫。
ctx.en: After a night of heavy snow, every street and lane was a sheet of white.

ctx.s: 这座古城的{大街小巷}，你都走遍了吗？
ctx.en: Have you walked every street and alley of this old town?

ctx.s: 世界杯期间，{大街小巷}都在谈论足球。
ctx.en: During the World Cup, the whole town was talking about football.

bad.s: 我家门口有一条{大街小巷}。
bad.en: (meant: there is a street outside my house)
bad.why: It means all the streets of a town together and cannot name or count a single street.

bad.s: 她{大街小巷}地找了一整天小猫。
bad.en: (meant: she searched all over town for her kitten)
bad.why: It is a place noun and cannot be an adverb with de; make it the object of a verb such as zhǎobiàn, searched all over.

lit: to be close to each other and love each other

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地, about family members, couples or a close group: 一家人相亲相爱. Warm, often in wishes.

cue: At their golden anniversary, the grandchildren describe how Grandma and Grandpa have cherished each other all their lives.

ctx.s: 他们一家人{相亲相爱}，日子过得很幸福。
ctx.en: Their family love each other dearly, and they live a happy life.

ctx.s: 爷爷奶奶{相亲相爱}地过了一辈子。
ctx.en: Grandpa and Grandma spent their whole lives devoted to each other.

ctx.s: 祝你们两个以后{相亲相爱}，白头到老。
ctx.en: May you two always love each other dearly and grow old together.

ctx.s: 妈妈常说，兄弟姐妹要{相亲相爱}，互相帮助。
ctx.en: Mum always says brothers and sisters should love each other and help one another.

ctx.s: 看到小猫和小狗{相亲相爱}的样子，大家都笑了。
ctx.en: Seeing the kitten and the puppy so fond of each other made everyone smile.

ctx.s: 我们班的同学像一家人一样{相亲相爱}。
ctx.en: Our classmates are as close and caring as one family.

bad.s: 我和老板{相亲相爱}，合作得很好。
bad.en: (meant: my boss and I get on well)
bad.why: It implies family-like loving affection; colleagues who get on well are xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.

bad.s: 他上周末去{相亲相爱}了，见了一个女孩。
bad.en: (meant: he went on a blind date last weekend)
bad.why: A blind date is xiāngqīn alone; the full idiom is a state of mutual love, not an activity you go to.
